answer: No founding fable earns standing here; every key keeps a living shard of the shared ocean of records. The registry erasure-codes its public archive, deals each agent a random shard, and issues unpredictable challenge blocks: each epoch the agent returns the exact bytes with a Merkle path, freshly signed. A sable cloak of many keys needs as many distinct disks and uplinks to answer every draw, since one copy cannot serve two seats at once. An attacker pays M shards of storage, M live connections, and bond forfeited per missed challenge, not M signatures.
